chat.a: Net sales were $3.07M in week 41, +5.0% vs last year. Units were −0.8%. The Harbor Parka, new this year, added $197K on its own — more than the whole increase.
All of it, and more, comes from one new product. Without the Harbor Parka, sales were −1.7% vs last year. Outerwear overall is +37.9%.

The Harbor Parka. It has 2.7 weeks of supply left, below the 4-week floor, and is selling about 820 units a week. That leaves a gap of about 4,380 units to an 8-week target, before any open orders or inbound stock, which this data doesn't hold.

chat.q: Who is buying the Harbor Parka?
chat.a: Mostly people new to the brand. Over the last four weeks, 55% of its orders came from new customers, against 32% for the brand overall. 47% of those new customers are Gen Z.
Weekend Straight. Sales are −16.5% vs last year and it has 19.2 weeks of supply, above the 16-week ceiling. Worth planning a markdown before the holidays.

chat.q: How are we doing with Gen Z?
chat.a: It is the fastest-growing group. Gen Z new customers are +50.6% vs last year in week 41, and they are now 28% of all new customers, up from 20%. The Harbor Parka skews most Gen Z: 48% of its new customers are Gen Z.

insights.headline: One new parka is carrying the week — the Harbor Parka added more than the whole increase, while denim keeps sliding.
insights.deck: Net sales were $3.07M, +5.0% vs LY — up from +2.7% over the prior four weeks (+2.3 pts). Outerwear is the engine at +7.1 pts, and nearly all of it is one product new this year: the Harbor Parka ($197K, +6.7 pts). Take it out and the week is −1.7%.
insights.why: Product leads. Outerwear is +37.9% vs LY, and the Harbor Parka is new to line — no LY comparison. Denim & Pants is the drag at −1.8 pts (−12.4%), and it isn't a one-week dip: Weekend Straight is −16.5%, against −14.4% over the prior four weeks. All 3 channels grew, so this is a product story, not a channel one.

actions.t: Chase the Harbor Parka before it sells out.
actions.b: 2.7 weeks of cover against a 4-week floor, selling about 820 a week. The gap to an 8-week target is about 4,380 units — indicative: the buyer nets off open POs and inbound, and checks lead time and size mix, before raising the order.

19.2 weeks of cover against a 16-week ceiling, with units −18.6% vs LY. About 7,700 units sit above the 16-week ceiling, and 27,180 above the 8-week target — hold open receipts until it is back under the ceiling.

actions.t: Turn the parka's new customers into repeat ones.
actions.b: 49% of Harbor Parka sales came from first-time customers, against 29% for the brand; 198 of its 412 new customers are Gen Z.

insights.bottom: This week's growth is one product deep. Is the Harbor Parka a one-season hit or the start of an outerwear franchise — and can supply keep up long enough to find out?

drills.q: What does the week look like without the Harbor Parka?
drills.b: $2.87M against $2.92M last year. The rest of Outerwear is only +1.9%; Denim & Pants takes −1.8 pts.

drills.q: Is denim a price problem or a demand problem?
drills.t: Demand — units are falling while price holds.
drills.b: Weekend Straight units are −18.6% vs LY with average price +2.6% ($88.78 vs $86.49), the same pattern as the prior four weeks (units −16.2%). This data has no markdown split, so the brief can't say whether a promotion would move it.

review.headline: Most friction this week is about time periods and definitions, not wrong numbers.
review.text: Buyers asked 148 questions. Only 1 answer had a number the checker flagged; the bigger theme is 7 questions where “October” or “last month” was read as the last 4 weeks. One theme needs a business definition before anyone can fix it.
